One more short step before you continue.

Pause detects the foreground app and opens a short learning exercise after your chosen interval. Window access is used only to identify the active app. Text, messages and taps are not saved. Data stays on your phone; the app has no internet access. You can disable the service here at any time.

Pause uses Accessibility to detect the foreground app and show a question at the right time.

Android gives this service access to window content. Our code reads only the app package name. It does not read text, record the screen, or tap buttons in other apps.

No data is sent over the internet. You can revoke access at any time.

On the next screen, find Pause — learning breaks (usually under Installed apps) and enable the service.

1. Choose apps and an interval.
2. Enable the Accessibility service.
3. Open a selected app and use it normally.

Only foreground time with the screen on and unlocked is counted. Pause does not track your gaze or distinguish feeds, messages and other sections of the same app.

When time is up, solve the question or use a skip. After revealing the answer, solve a different question or use a skip. Choose this behavior in subject settings; the skip allowance and delay still apply. You may go home; the question will wait when you return.

On Samsung, if Android blocks the service, open Pause app info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, if available. Then enable the service again.

If the service stops, check battery restrictions and sleeping apps. After force-stopping Pause, reopen it and check the service.

This is a voluntary tool: you can disable or uninstall it. There is no answer deadline.

Revealing an answer does not count as solving it. A new question keeps the same break step. Skipping ends the break and uses this app’s allowance; the skip delay still applies. If skipping is unavailable, you can solve a new question.
After revealing: a new question or a skip from your allowance. An exposed answer cannot count as solved.
You have seen the answer, but the question is not solved. Try a different question at the same break step.
Use a skip from your allowance to return to watching. If you want to save it or have none left, solve a new question.
Choose: solve a different question at the same step, or use a skip to end this break.
In a real break, revealing requires a new question or a skip from your allowance. Here you can try another question or close the preview.

With playback unchanged, players control the music themselves: it may resume when a question covers the feed.\n\nPause players asks players to stop when a question opens. Music is not automatically restarted afterwards; you may need to press Play. Behavior depends on the player. Calls and volume settings are unchanged.
